slowest_experiments.experiment: Measure complete durable Python transactions with fixed work units
Bind fourteen tasks and repair historical consumer input isolation
Qualify direct state after immutable consumer and barrier coverage repairs
Reconcile fourteen terminal outcomes with immutable historical consumers
Measure causal small-head updates through durable direct serving

summary: Milestone 2026.10.724 completed 12 experiments (0 compute-bound, 12 synthesis-only) across 181.5 total wall-time minutes (averaging 15 minutes per experiment) reconstructed from disk-mtime fallback data. Execution wall time was led by synthesis-only tasks—measuring complete durable Python transactions with fixed work units (62.23 minutes), binding fourteen tasks and repairing historical consumer input isolation (32.68 minutes), qualifying direct state after immutable consumer and barrier coverage repairs (25.32 minutes), reconciling fourteen terminal outcomes with immutable historical consumers (21.24 minutes), and measuring causal small-head updates through durable direct serving (16.49 minutes). With compute_bound_experiments_count at 0 and gpu_idle_on_compute_bound_tasks recorded as null, the point-in-time monitor reading of 0% GPU utilization (4MB allocated) on both NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3090 GPUs represents expected idle behavior for non-GPU synthesis workloads rather than an accelerator bottleneck, and no multi-model parallel workload required DualGPURunner dispatch.
bottlenecks_identified: Synthesis-only tasks accounted for the entirety of milestone execution time (all 12 completed experiments totaling 181.5 wall-time minutes), led by Python transaction measurement (62.23 minutes), task binding and input isolation repair (32.68 minutes), direct state qualification (25.32 minutes), fourteen-outcome reconciliation (21.24 minutes), and causal small-head update measurement (16.49 minutes).

meta_reflection: Across 12 completed experiments and 181.5 minutes of milestone wall time, execution was entirely dominated by synthesis-only tasks averaging 15 minutes per experiment, with zero compute-bound tasks executed and gpu_idle_on_compute_bound_tasks recorded as null. Observed 0% GPU utilization (4MB allocated) on both NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3090 GPUs reflected expected idle state for non-GPU synthesis workloads rather than an accelerator bottleneck, correctly bypassing DualGPURunner dispatch. Operational improvements should focus on incremental receipt caching for unchanged upstream artifacts and granular intra-phase telemetry for multi-minute synthesis tasks, with estimated time savings conservatively held at 0% until empirically validated.
